page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core, supported by 64.0 GB of memory, which translates to 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate exceptional memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score reaching the top tier (top 10%) and large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks placing in the top 25% with 296.82 GB/sec read and 133.57 GB/sec write speeds. Compute performance is robust, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores in the top 25%, alongside strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, while small-model LLM inference and medium-model text generation perform at average levels, prompt processing for medium 7B models is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%.

Given its ARM64 architecture and dedicated physical cores, the m8gd.4xlarge offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads that do not require x86-specific instruction sets. The combination of high-speed local NVMe storage and strong database operation benchmarks makes it highly suitable for database hosting, caching layers, and general-purpose web serving. It is also well-suited for text processing and software compilation, though it is less optimal for heavy LLM prompt processing.
